intro: Searching for a damp surveyor near you usually means something in your home has started to smell musty, show tide marks or feel cold and clammy, and you want to know why before anyone sells you a treatment. It helps to have someone independent look at the actual cause, whether that turns out to be condensation, a leak or rising damp. iComply is a free introduction service: you tell us what you need, and we introduce you to a suitable UK surveyor who quotes you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a damp surveyor near them usually need
need_lead: Most people want an honest diagnosis of what is causing the damp before they commit to any work or expense.
needs: You have noticed a damp patch, peeling paint or a dark tidemark on a wall and want to know whether it is rising damp or something else.
There is a musty smell or condensation on the windows that keeps coming back, and you want to understand the real cause rather than just wipe it away.
A treatment company has already told you what needs doing, and you would like an independent view before agreeing to it.
You are buying or selling a home and a damp issue has shown up that needs explaining properly.
You have had damp work done before and the problem has returned, so you want a fresh diagnosis of what is going on.
context_heading: Why an independent survey matters with damp
context: Damp has several possible causes, and condensation is a common one, so a diagnosis that jumps straight to a costly treatment can miss the point. An independent damp surveyor looks at the cause before any treatment is priced, which helps you avoid a sales-led answer.

Many surveyors belong to the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS), and RICS-regulated firms must follow professional standards, hold insurance and offer a complaints process. Chartered surveyors use the letters MRICS or FRICS, and damp and timber specialists may belong to the Property Care Association (PCA), so it is worth asking about qualifications.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Where the damp is showing, such as a wall, floor, ceiling or around the windows.
What you have noticed, including any musty smell, tide marks, peeling paint or mould.
How long the problem has been there and whether it comes and goes with the weather.
Whether any damp treatment has already been carried out and whether the problem returned.
Whether you are buying, selling or staying in the property, as this affects what you need.
Your postcode or area so we can introduce you to a surveyor who covers where you are.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the damp surveyor
questions: What qualifications and professional memberships do you hold for damp surveying?
Will the survey be independent of any treatment work you or your firm might carry out?
What kind of report will I receive, and what will it cover?
How will you work out whether the cause is condensation, a leak or rising damp?
Will you explain the findings to me directly and put the recommendations in writing?
What is the cost of the survey, and is it quoted on application?

faqs.q: How do I find a damp surveyor near me?
faqs.a: Start by telling iComply where you are and what you have noticed, and we will introduce you to a suitable UK surveyor who covers your area. You can also check the RICS directory for chartered surveyors and look for PCA membership among damp specialists.

faqs.q: Is the damp always rising damp?
faqs.a: No. Condensation is a common cause, and leaks and other issues can also be responsible. An independent surveyor should diagnose the actual cause before any treatment is recommended.

faqs.q: Why does independence matter for a damp survey?
faqs.a: If the same firm diagnoses the damp and sells the treatment, there is a risk the diagnosis is led by the sale. An independent survey gives you a view of the cause before you decide what to do.

faqs.q: What should I have ready before the surveyor visits?
faqs.a: It helps to note where the damp appears, any smells or mould, and whether treatment has been done before. Mentioning whether you are buying, selling or staying also helps the surveyor understand what you need.
